q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT a.bar, b.bar FROM serves AS a RIGHT OUTER JOIN serves AS b ON a.bar <> b.bar AND a.beer = b.beer
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT a.bar, b.bar FROM serves AS a RIGHT OUTER JOIN serves AS b ON a.bar <> b.bar AND a.beer = b.beer
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('Bar A', 'Address 1'), ('Bar B', 'Address 2'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('Beer X', 'Brewer Y'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('Bar A', 'Beer X', 10.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve a unique beer (no other bar serves the same beer) and another bar that does not serve that beer. Q2, on the other hand, uses a right outer join to find pairs of bars that serve the same beer, excluding the case where the bars are the same.
counterexample_dsp: Create two bars, 'Bar A' and 'Bar B', where 'Bar A' serves beer 'Beer X' and 'Bar B' does not serve 'Beer X'.
